title: [Model] Mamba2 Prefill Performance Tweaks: Fixing Flurry of Unnecessary Memory Copies  (#14778)
gain_evidence: The total token throughput improved by about 8%.

experiments.name: mamba2_prefill_layer_latency
experiments.workload: Bamba-9B on H100-80GB, offline mode, batch size 64, short prompt; per-Mamba-prefill-layer latency as seen in the Nsight Systems trace. Compared against the pre-change mamba_mixer2 forward.
experiments.note: Diff touches only vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/mamba_mixer2.py: eliminates/fuses two phases of unnecessary per-layer memory copies identified in an nsys trace. Headline number is the author body claim: the fix reduces the prefill mamba layer latency from 5ms to 3ms for the batch=64 short-prompt case. (Author also reports an E2E benchmark_serving run: total token throughput 1460.17 -> 1589.37 tok/s, ~8%.)

reported.scope: per-Mamba-prefill-layer wall latency from an nsys trace (Bamba-9B, batch=64, short prompt), a GPU-kernel-level measurement
reported.scale_short: Author's 5->3ms is a single Mamba prefill layer read off an nsys GPU trace, not a CPU-isolatable op. TO MAKE 1:1: on a GPU box profile one mamba_mixer2 prefill forward (Bamba-9B, batch=64) before vs after merge_sha with nsys and compare per-layer latency.
reported.scale_note: The win is removal of GPU memory copies, so it only manifests on-GPU and cannot be reproduced on a CPU microbench. The 5ms->3ms is one layer in one trace; the companion E2E serving run (ShareGPT, 1000 reqs, H100) showed ~8% total tok/s (1460.17->1589.37), diluted by the rest of the model. Author notes another similar sequential loop remains unfixed because the test case did not hit that control path.
